1	"""Exact multi-generation selection gap as a Markov chain on the score lattice.
2	
3	``evaluation_game_feedback.selection_inflation`` gives the one-generation
4	over-report from keeping the best of ``K`` candidates scored on one reused set
5	of ``n`` items.  ``paper/evaluation_feedback_insertions.md`` records that
6	accumulation of that gap across generations "is a simulation result, not an
7	exact one".  This module makes it exact.  Nothing here calls a model, samples,
8	or reads the simulations; every number is a ``Fraction`` produced by a finite
9	dynamic programme over a finite Markov chain or by finite enumeration.
10	
11	The chain (null model: no true improvement)
12	-------------------------------------------
13	* Vertices (states): the incumbent's realized count ``c`` on the reused set,
14	  ``c in {0, ..., n}``.
15	* Each generation draws ``K`` candidates i.i.d. and independent of the
16	  incumbent.  Candidate ``k`` scores ``C_k ~ Bin(n, p)`` on the reused set
17	  (each item an independent Bernoulli(p)).  Write ``M = max_k C_k``.
18	* Policy (acceptance rule): accept the best candidate iff ``M > c + t(c)`` for
19	  a threshold function ``t: {0..n} -> N``.  ``t == 0`` is naive reuse.
20	  ``t(c) = floor(z * sqrt(c (n - c) / n))`` is the exact integer form of the
21	  PREREG gate ``GATE_Z * sqrt(p (1 - p) / n) * n`` with ``p = c / n``: the
22	  count difference ``M - c`` is an integer ``d``, and ``d > x`` for real ``x``
23	  iff ``d >= floor(x) + 1``.  The floor of the square root of a rational is
24	  computed exactly with ``math.isqrt``.
25	* Edges: ``c -> j`` with probability ``P(M = j)`` for every ``j > c + t(c)``,
26	  and the self-loop ``c -> c`` with the remaining mass ``F(c + t(c))^K``,
27	  where ``F`` is the binomial CDF with ``F(j) = 1`` for ``j >= n``.  Every
28	  other edge has probability zero, so the transition graph is a DAG of upward
29	  edges plus self-loops; its sinks, the states with ``c + t(c) >= n``, are the
30	  absorbing states.
31	* Initial state: the incumbent's own count on the reused set,
32	  ``c_0 ~ Bin(n, p)``.
33	* Reported score after ``G`` generations: ``c_G / n``.  Readout value under
34	  the null: ``p``.  Readout gap: ``rho_G = E[c_G] / n - p``.
35	
36	The drift model (``drift_trajectory``) adds a level index for the incumbent's
37	true success probability on a finite lattice ``p_0 + i * step`` capped at one,
38	so that true gains and phantom gains can be separated exactly.
39	
40	Version 0.2 adds three pieces.  (A) Proven upper bounds on the naive gap
41	(Hoeffding and Bernstein maximal inequalities), compared with the exact DP
42	in floating point under a stated tolerance.  (B) The mutation chain
43	(``mutation_candidate_law`` and friends): a candidate copies the incumbent's
44	outcome on each item with probability ``1 - q`` and redraws it as
45	Bernoulli(p) with probability ``q``, which is an exact model of
46	item-correlated candidates and still a Markov chain on the count.  (C) The
47	one-generation gate-versus-naive theorem under true gains
48	(``one_step_gap_change``) and finite checks of how its sign chains across
49	generations.
50	
51	Version 0.3 adds (D) the dominance question: whether the naive chain is
52	above every gated chain in both expected count and expected true value at
53	every generation under a fixed gain.  For the true value this is a theorem
54	(Proposition 8, proof sketched before ``drift_kernel``; every threshold
55	rule, every non-decreasing level function, every state); for the count it
56	is a finite result of an exact 972-cell search with no counterexample
57	(``dominance_sweep_fixture``) plus witnesses showing why the standard
58	proof routes fail (``dominance_structure_fixture``).  The search uses an
59	exact integer-numerator propagation (``drift_expectations``) and the exact
60	``g -> infinity`` limit (``drift_limit``).
61	
62	Boundaries
63	----------
64	The independent chain has candidates independent of the incumbent; the
65	mutation chain correlates them item by item through one parameter ``q``,
66	which is not an exact image of ``sim.js``'s latent rotation.  ``n`` is fixed,
67	labels are clean, and every statement concerns distributions and
68	expectations, not sample paths.  Bounds that involve ``ln`` or ``sqrt`` are
69	floats and are compared to exact values under ``BOUND_TOLERANCE``.
70	"""
71	
72	from __future__ import annotations
73	
74	from fractions import Fraction as Q
75	from itertools import product
76	from math import isqrt, lcm, log, sqrt
77	
78	from spiral_ln.evaluation_game_feedback import (_binomial_pmf, divergence_flags,
79	                                                selection_inflation)
80	
81	REPORT_MODES = ("selection_block", "separate_block")
82	_BRUTE_FORCE_BIT_LIMIT = 16
83	_BRUTE_FORCE_GAIN_COMBINATIONS = 64
84	
85	
86	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	# validation helpers
88	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	
90	def _check_items_candidates(items, candidates):
91	    if (type(items) is not int or type(candidates) is not int
92	            or items < 1 or candidates < 1):
93	        raise ValueError("items and candidates must be positive integers")
94	
95	
96	def _check_probability(p, name="p"):
97	    if type(p) is bool or not isinstance(p, (int, Q)) or not 0 <= p <= 1:
98	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a Fraction in [0, 1]")
99	    return Q(p)
100	
101	
102	def _check_generations(generations):
103	    if type(generations) is not int or generations < 0:
104	        raise ValueError("generations must be a non-negative integer")
105	
106	
107	def _check_threshold(threshold, items):
108	    try:
109	        threshold = tuple(threshold)
110	    except TypeError:
111	        raise ValueError("threshold must be a sequence") from None
112	    if (len(threshold) != items + 1
113	            or any(type(t) is not int or t < 0 for t in threshold)):
114	        raise ValueError("threshold must give one non-negative integer per state")
115	    return threshold
116	
117	
118	def _check_distribution(distribution, items):
119	    try:
120	        distribution = [Q(mass) for mass in distribution]
121	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
122	        raise ValueError("distribution must be a sequence of rationals") from None
123	    if (len(distribution) != items + 1 or any(mass < 0 for mass in distribution)
124	            or sum(distribution) != 1):
125	        raise ValueError("distribution must be a probability vector over the states")
126	    return distribution
127	
128	
129	def _check_gain(gain):
130	    if not isinstance(gain, dict) or not gain:
131	        raise ValueError("gain must be a non-empty mapping from step multiples to probabilities")
132	    checked = {}
133	    for multiple, mass in gain.items():
134	        if type(multiple) is not int or multiple < 0:
135	            raise ValueError("gain multiples must be non-negative integers")
136	        checked[multiple] = _check_probability(mass, "gain probability")
137	    if sum(checked.values()) != 1:
138	        raise ValueError("gain probabilities must sum to one")
139	    return checked
140	
141	
142	def _check_gain_schedule(gain, generations):
143	    """A single mapping applies to every generation; a sequence gives one
144	    mapping per generation."""
145	
146	    if isinstance(gain, dict):
147	        return [_check_gain(gain)] * generations
148	    try:
149	        schedule = list(gain)
150	    except TypeError:
151	        raise ValueError("gain must be a mapping or a sequence of mappings") from None
152	    if len(schedule) != generations:
153	        raise ValueError("gain schedule must have one entry per generation")
154	    return [_check_gain(entry) for entry in schedule]
155	
156	
157	def decaying_gain_schedule(generations, q0, ratio, multiple=1) -> list[dict[int, Q]]:
158	    """Two-point schedule: in generation ``g`` (1-based) a candidate carries
159	    gain ``multiple`` with probability ``q0 * ratio**(g - 1)`` and gain zero
160	    otherwise.  A finite-lattice analogue of the simulation's decaying
161	    general-change scale ``0.06 * 0.95**(g - 1)``."""
162	
163	    _check_generations(generations)
164	    q0 = _check_probability(q0, "q0")
165	    ratio = _check_probability(ratio, "ratio")
166	    if type(multiple) is not int or multiple < 1:
167	        raise ValueError("multiple must be a positive integer")
168	    schedule = []
169	    for g in range(generations):
170	        q = q0 * ratio**g
171	        schedule.append({0: 1 - q, multiple: q} if q else {0: Q(1)})
172	    return schedule
173	
174	
175	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
176	# binomial building blocks
177	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
178	
179	def binomial_cdf(items: int, p: Q) -> list[Q]:
180	    running, cdf = Q(0), []
181	    for mass in _binomial_pmf(items, p):
182	        running += mass
183	        cdf.append(running)
184	    return cdf
185	
186	
187	def best_of_pmf(items: int, candidates: int, p: Q) -> list[Q]:
188	    """Law of ``max`` of ``candidates`` i.i.d. ``Bin(items, p)`` draws."""
189	
190	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
191	    p = _check_probability(p)
192	    cdf = binomial_cdf(items, p)
193	    return [cdf[j]**candidates - (cdf[j - 1]**candidates if j else Q(0))
194	            for j in range(items + 1)]
195	
196	
197	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
198	# policies
199	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
200	
201	def naive_threshold(items: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
202	    """``t == 0``: accept whenever the best candidate beats the incumbent."""
203	
204	    if type(items) is not int or items < 1:
205	        raise ValueError("items must be a positive integer")
206	    return (0,) * (items + 1)
207	
208	
209	def gate_threshold(items: int, z) -> tuple[int, ...]:
210	    """``t(c) = floor(z * sqrt(c (n - c) / n))`` computed exactly.
211	
212	    With ``q = z^2 c (n - c) / n = a / b`` in lowest terms,
213	    ``floor(sqrt(q)) = isqrt(a b) // b``, because ``floor(x / b) =
214	    floor(floor(x) / b)`` for real ``x >= 0`` and integer ``b >= 1``.
215	    """
216	
217	    if type(items) is not int or items < 1:
218	        raise ValueError("items must be a positive integer")
219	    if type(z) is bool or not isinstance(z, (int, Q)) or z < 0:
220	        raise ValueError("z must be a non-negative Fraction")
221	    thresholds = []
222	    for c in range(items + 1):
223	        q = Q(z)**2 * c * (items - c) / items
224	        thresholds.append(isqrt(q.numerator * q.denominator) // q.denominator)
225	    return tuple(thresholds)
226	
227	
228	def false_acceptance_probability(items, candidates, p, threshold) -> tuple[Q, ...]:
229	    """``alpha(c) = P(M > c + t(c)) = 1 - F(min(n, c + t(c)))^K``.
230	
231	    Under the null every acceptance is false, so this is the per-generation
232	    false-acceptance probability from state ``c``.
233	    """
234	
235	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
236	    p = _check_probability(p)
237	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
238	    cdf = binomial_cdf(items, p)
239	    return tuple(1 - cdf[min(items, c + threshold[c])]**candidates
240	                 for c in range(items + 1))
241	
242	
243	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
244	# null chain: kernel, DP, trajectory
245	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
246	
247	def transition_kernel(items, candidates, p, threshold) -> list[list[Q]]:
248	    """Row ``c`` is the law of the next state from ``c``.
249	
250	    ``kernel[c][c] = F(cap)^K`` with ``cap = min(n, c + t(c))``;
251	    ``kernel[c][j] = P(M = j)`` for ``j > cap``; zero elsewhere.
252	    """
253	
254	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
255	    p = _check_probability(p)
256	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
257	    cdf = binomial_cdf(items, p)
258	    best = best_of_pmf(items, candidates, p)
259	    rows = []
260	    for c in range(items + 1):
261	        cap = min(items, c + threshold[c])
262	        row = [Q(0)] * (items + 1)
263	        row[c] = cdf[cap]**candidates
264	        for j in range(cap + 1, items + 1):
265	            row[j] = best[j]
266	        rows.append(row)
267	    return rows
268	
269	
270	def state_distribution(items, candidates, p, threshold, generations,
271	                       initial=None) -> list[list[Q]]:
272	    """Exact law of the state after ``0, 1, ..., generations`` generations.
273	
274	    ``initial`` defaults to ``Bin(items, p)``: the incumbent is scored on the
275	    reused set before any selection.  A point mass models an incumbent whose
276	    count is known.
277	    """
278	
279	    _check_generations(generations)
280	    kernel = transition_kernel(items, candidates, p, threshold)
281	    current = (_binomial_pmf(items, Q(p)) if initial is None
282	               else _check_distribution(initial, items))
283	    return _propagate(kernel, current, generations)
284	
285	
286	def _propagate(kernel, current, generations):
287	    history = [current]
288	    for _ in range(generations):
289	        following = [Q(0)] * len(current)
290	        for c, mass in enumerate(current):
291	            if mass:
292	                for j, prob in enumerate(kernel[c]):
293	                    if prob:
294	                        following[j] += mass * prob
295	        history.append(following)
296	        current = following
297	    return history
298	
299	
300	def reuse_trajectory(items, candidates, p, threshold, generations) -> dict[str, object]:
301	    """Per-generation expectations for the reused-set chain under the null.
302	
303	    ``expected_true`` is the constant ``p`` so that the same readers work on
304	    null and drift trajectories.  ``acceptance_probability[g - 1]`` is the
305	    probability that generation ``g`` accepts, every acceptance being false.
306	    """
307	
308	    history = state_distribution(items, candidates, p, threshold, generations)
309	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
310	    alpha = false_acceptance_probability(items, candidates, p, threshold)
311	    reported = [sum(c * mass for c, mass in enumerate(dist)) / items for dist in history]
312	    acceptance = [sum(mass * alpha[c] for c, mass in enumerate(dist)) for dist in history[:-1]]
313	    p = Q(p)
314	    return {
315	        "items": items, "candidates": candidates, "p": p, "threshold": threshold,
316	        "generations": generations,
317	        "expected_reported": reported, "expected_true": [p] * (generations + 1),
318	        "readout_value": p, "readout_gap": [value - p for value in reported],
319	        "acceptance_probability": acceptance,
320	        "expected_acceptances": sum(acceptance, Q(0)),
321	        "ceiling_mass": history[-1][items],
322	        "absorbing_states": tuple(c for c in range(items + 1) if c + threshold[c] >= items),
323	        "final_distribution": history[-1],
324	    }
325	
326	
327	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
328	# closed forms for naive reuse (t == 0)
329	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
330	
331	def naive_closed_form(items, candidates, p, generations) -> dict[str, Q]:
332	    """Naive reuse after ``G`` generations is the max of ``G K + 1`` draws.
333	
334	    With ``t == 0`` the state satisfies ``c_g = max(c_{g-1}, M_g)``, so
335	    ``c_G = max(c_0, M_1, ..., M_G)`` is the maximum of the initial incumbent's
336	    draw and all ``G K`` candidate draws: ``G K + 1`` i.i.d. ``Bin(n, p)``
337	    counts.  The one-generation formula applies with ``K`` replaced by
338	    ``G K + 1``; the initial incumbent counts as one draw because it is
339	    scored on the reused set like every candidate.
340	    """
341	
342	    _check_generations(generations)
343	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
344	    return selection_inflation(items, generations * candidates + 1, p)
345	
346	
347	def running_max_from_point(items, candidates, p, generations, start) -> Q:
348	    """``E[max(c_0, X)]`` for a known incumbent count ``c_0`` and ``X`` the
349	    max of ``G K`` candidate draws; the naive chain started at a point."""
350	
351	    _check_generations(generations)
352	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
353	    if type(start) is not int or not 0 <= start <= items:
354	        raise ValueError("start must be a state")
355	    draws = generations * candidates
356	    if draws == 0:
357	        return Q(start)
358	    pmf = best_of_pmf(items, draws, p)
359	    return sum(max(start, j) * mass for j, mass in enumerate(pmf))

365	    _check_generations(generations)
366	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)

372	# proven upper bounds for naive reuse (floats; compared under a tolerance)
373	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
374	
375	BOUND_TOLERANCE = 1e-12
376	
377	
378	def naive_gap_bounds(items, candidates, p, generations) -> dict[str, object]:
379	    """Upper bounds on ``rho_G`` under naive reuse, from maximal inequalities.
380	
381	    ``c_G`` is the max of ``m = G K + 1`` i.i.d. ``Bin(n, p)`` draws
382	    (``naive_closed_form``).  Write ``Y_i = X_i - n p``.
383	
384	    Hoeffding.  Each centred Bernoulli lies in an interval of length one, so
385	    Hoeffding's lemma gives ``E exp(lam (B - p)) <= exp(lam^2 / 8)``, and by
386	    independence over items ``E exp(lam Y_i) <= exp(lam^2 n / 8)``.  The
387	    maximal inequality ``E max_i Y_i <= (1 / lam) ln sum_i E exp(lam Y_i)``
388	    (Jensen, then ``max <= sum`` on the exponentials) gives
389	    ``E max_i Y_i <= (ln m) / lam + lam n / 8`` for every ``lam > 0``, and
390	    ``lam = sqrt(8 ln m / n)`` makes the right side ``sqrt(n ln m / 2)``.
391	    Dividing by ``n``: ``rho_G <= sqrt(ln m / (2 n))``.
392	
393	    Bernstein.  For a centred variable ``Z`` with ``|Z| <= 1`` and variance
394	    ``v``, ``E exp(lam Z) <= exp(v (e^lam - 1 - lam))``, and
395	    ``e^lam - 1 - lam <= lam^2 / (2 (1 - lam / 3))`` for ``0 < lam < 3``
396	    (``k! >= 2 * 3^(k-2)``).  Over ``n`` items ``v = n p (1 - p)``, and the
397	    maximal inequality with ``lam = 1 / (1/3 + sqrt(v / (2 ln m)))`` gives
398	    ``E max_i Y_i <= sqrt(2 v ln m) + (ln m) / 3`` (Boucheron, Lugosi and
399	    Massart, Corollary 2.6).  Dividing by ``n``:
400	    ``rho_G <= sqrt(2 p (1 - p) ln m / n) + ln m / (3 n)``.
401	
402	    ``gaussian_scale`` is the leading term ``sqrt(2 p (1 - p) ln m / n)``,
403	    the Gaussian extreme-value scale the earlier remark used.  Both bounds
404	    are proven for every ``n, K, p, G``; both grow without bound in ``G``
405	    while ``rho_G <= 1 - p``, so they are loose for large ``G`` at fixed
406	    ``n``.  The values are floats (``math.log``, ``math.sqrt``); compare with
407	    exact gaps under ``BOUND_TOLERANCE``.
408	    """
409	
410	    _check_generations(generations)
411	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
412	    p = _check_probability(p)
413	    draws = generations * candidates + 1
414	    log_draws = log(draws)
415	    variance = float(p * (1 - p))
416	    gaussian = sqrt(2 * log_draws * variance / items)
417	    return {"draws": draws, "log_draws": log_draws,
418	            "hoeffding": sqrt(log_draws / (2 * items)),
419	            "bernstein": gaussian + log_draws / (3 * items),
420	            "gaussian_scale": gaussian,
421	            "lattice_cap": float(1 - p)}

428	def fresh_block_reported(items, candidates, p, threshold) -> dict[str, Q]:
429	    """One generation on a fresh block, reporting on that same block.
430	
431	    The incumbent is re-scored on the fresh block, ``I ~ Bin(n, p)``,
432	    independently of the ``K`` candidates.  The reported count is ``M`` if
433	    ``M > I + t(I)`` and ``I`` otherwise.  With ``t == 0`` this is
434	    ``max(I, M)``, the max of ``K + 1`` draws, i.e.
435	    ``selection_inflation(n, K + 1, p)``.
436	    """
437	
438	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
439	    p = _check_probability(p)
440	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
441	    pmf, cdf = _binomial_pmf(items, p), binomial_cdf(items, p)
442	    best = best_of_pmf(items, candidates, p)
443	    expected = Q(0)
444	    for c, mass in enumerate(pmf):
445	        cap = min(items, c + threshold[c])
446	        expected += mass * (c * cdf[cap]**candidates
447	                            + sum(j * best[j] for j in range(cap + 1, items + 1)))
448	    reported = expected / items
449	    return {"expected_reported": reported, "readout_value": p, "readout_gap": reported - p}

452	def fresh_trajectory(items, candidates, p, threshold, generations, report_on) -> dict[str, object]:
453	    """Per-generation expected reported score when every generation scores on
454	    a fresh block.
455	
456	    Under the null the incumbent's identity carries no score, so the arm's
457	    state space is a single point and each generation's reported score is an
458	    independent copy.  ``separate_block``: the accepted controller is scored
459	    on a second fresh block, whose count is ``Bin(n, p)`` whatever was
460	    selected, so the expected reported score is ``p`` at every generation.
461	    ``selection_block``: generation ``g >= 1`` reports ``fresh_block_reported``
462	    and generation ``0`` reports the incumbent's own fresh count, mean ``p``.
463	    """
464	
465	    _check_generations(generations)
466	    if report_on not in REPORT_MODES:
467	        raise ValueError("unknown report mode")
468	    p = _check_probability(p)
469	    if report_on == "separate_block":
470	        _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
471	        _check_threshold(threshold, items)
472	        reported = [p] * (generations + 1)
473	    else:
474	        one = fresh_block_reported(items, candidates, p, threshold)["expected_reported"]
475	        reported = [p] + [one] * generations
476	    return {"report_on": report_on, "expected_reported": reported,
477	            "expected_true": [p] * (generations + 1), "readout_value": p,
478	            "readout_gap": [value - p for value in reported]}

482	# mutation chain: candidates correlated with the incumbent item by item
483	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
484	
485	def _check_state(c, items):
486	    if type(c) is not int or not 0 <= c <= items:
487	        raise ValueError("c must be a state in 0..items")
488	
489	
490	def mutation_candidate_law(items, p, q, c) -> list[Q]:
491	    """Law of one candidate's count given the incumbent's count ``c``.
492	
493	    On each item, independently, the candidate copies the incumbent's
494	    outcome with probability ``1 - q`` and otherwise redraws it as
495	    Bernoulli(p).  An item the incumbent got right is lost iff it is redrawn
496	    and fails, probability ``q (1 - p)``; an item the incumbent got wrong is
497	    gained iff it is redrawn and succeeds, probability ``q p``.  Hence
498	    ``count = c - L + U`` with ``L ~ Bin(c, q (1 - p))`` and
499	    ``U ~ Bin(n - c, q p)`` independent.  The law depends on the incumbent's
500	    outcome vector only through ``c`` because items are exchangeable and
501	    the perturbation is the same on every item, so the chain on ``c`` is
502	    Markov.  ``q = 1`` gives ``Bin(c, p) + Bin(n - c, p) = Bin(n, p)``, the
503	    independent chain; ``q = 0`` gives the point mass at ``c``.  Marginally
504	    (incumbent ``~ Bin(n, p)``) a candidate is again ``Bin(n, p)``, with
505	    per-item outcome correlation ``1 - q`` to the incumbent.
506	    """
507	
508	    if type(items) is not int or items < 1:
509	        raise ValueError("items must be a positive integer")
510	    p = _check_probability(p)
511	    q = _check_probability(q, "q")
512	    _check_state(c, items)
513	    loss = _binomial_pmf(c, q * (1 - p))
514	    gain = _binomial_pmf(items - c, q * p)
515	    law = [Q(0)] * (items + 1)
516	    for lost, mass_lost in enumerate(loss):
517	        for gained, mass_gained in enumerate(gain):
518	            law[c - lost + gained] += mass_lost * mass_gained
519	    return law
520	
521	
522	def mutation_transition_kernel(items, candidates, p, q, threshold) -> list[list[Q]]:
523	    """As ``transition_kernel`` with ``K`` i.i.d. mutation candidates given
524	    ``c``: ``kernel[c][c] = F_c(cap)^K``, ``kernel[c][j] = P(M = j)`` for
525	    ``j > cap``, where ``F_c`` is the CDF of ``mutation_candidate_law``."""
526	
527	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
528	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
529	    rows = []
530	    for c in range(items + 1):
531	        cdf, running = [], Q(0)
532	        for mass in mutation_candidate_law(items, p, q, c):
533	            running += mass
534	            cdf.append(running)
535	        cap = min(items, c + threshold[c])
536	        row = [Q(0)] * (items + 1)
537	        row[c] = cdf[cap]**candidates
538	        for j in range(cap + 1, items + 1):
539	            row[j] = cdf[j]**candidates - cdf[j - 1]**candidates
540	        rows.append(row)
541	    return rows
542	
543	
544	def mutation_state_distribution(items, candidates, p, q, threshold, generations,
545	                                initial=None) -> list[list[Q]]:
546	    """Exact state law after ``0..generations`` generations of the mutation
547	    chain; ``initial`` defaults to ``Bin(items, p)``."""
548	
549	    _check_generations(generations)
550	    kernel = mutation_transition_kernel(items, candidates, p, q, threshold)
551	    current = (_binomial_pmf(items, Q(p)) if initial is None
552	               else _check_distribution(initial, items))
553	    return _propagate(kernel, current, generations)

556	def mutation_trajectory(items, candidates, p, q, threshold, generations) -> dict[str, object]:
557	    """Per-generation expectations for the mutation chain under the null.
558	
559	    Acceptance never lowers ``c`` (it requires ``M > c + t(c) >= c``), so
560	    ``c_g`` is pointwise non-decreasing and ``rho_g`` is non-decreasing in
561	    ``g`` and bounded by ``1 - p`` for every ``q``.  Unlike the independent
562	    chain, ``c_G`` is not a running maximum of i.i.d. draws: the candidate
563	    law moves with the state, so Proposition 1 has no analogue here.
564	    """
565	
566	    history = mutation_state_distribution(items, candidates, p, q, threshold, generations)
567	    kernel = mutation_transition_kernel(items, candidates, p, q, threshold)
568	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
569	    alpha = tuple(1 - kernel[c][c] for c in range(items + 1))
570	    reported = [sum(c * mass for c, mass in enumerate(dist)) / items for dist in history]
571	    acceptance = [sum(mass * alpha[c] for c, mass in enumerate(dist)) for dist in history[:-1]]
572	    p, q = Q(p), Q(q)
573	    return {
574	        "items": items, "candidates": candidates, "p": p, "q": q, "threshold": threshold,
575	        "generations": generations,
576	        "expected_reported": reported, "expected_true": [p] * (generations + 1),
577	        "readout_value": p, "readout_gap": [value - p for value in reported],
578	        "acceptance_probability": acceptance,
579	        "acceptance_by_state": alpha,
580	        "expected_acceptances": sum(acceptance, Q(0)),
581	        "ceiling_mass": history[-1][items],
582	        "final_distribution": history[-1],
583	    }

587	# drift model: true gains on a finite lattice
588	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
589	
590	def drift_levels(p0, step) -> tuple[Q, ...]:
591	    """Lattice ``p(i) = min(1, p0 + i * step)``, ending at the first level
592	    that reaches one; the index is clamped there."""
593	
594	    p0 = _check_probability(p0, "p0")
595	    if type(step) is bool or not isinstance(step, (int, Q)) or step <= 0:
596	        raise ValueError("step must be a positive Fraction")
597	    levels, index = [], 0
598	    while p0 + index * step < 1:
599	        levels.append(p0 + index * step)
600	        index += 1
601	    levels.append(Q(1))
602	    return tuple(levels)
603	
604	
605	def drift_trajectory(items, candidates, p0, step, gain, threshold, generations) -> dict[str, object]:
606	    """Exact chain on ``(count, level)`` with true gains.
607	
608	    The incumbent at level ``i`` has true success probability ``p(i)``.  Each
609	    candidate independently draws a gain multiple ``m`` from ``gain``
610	    (``{m: probability}``), has true probability ``p(min(top, i + m))`` and
611	    count ``C ~ Bin(n, p(.))``.  ``M`` is the best count; the policy accepts
612	    iff ``M > c + t(c)``; on acceptance the state becomes ``(M, i + m*)``
613	    where ``m*`` is the gain of the accepted candidate.  Ties among candidates
614	    go to the first index, which for exchangeable candidates gives the
615	    conditional law ``P(m | C = M)``; so
616	    ``P(M = j, m* = m) = P(M = j) * gain[m] * Bin(n, p(i + m))(j) / mix(j)``
617	    with ``mix`` the candidate count mixture.
618	
619	    Reported value: ``E[c_g] / n``.  True value: ``E[p(i_g)]``.  Readout gap:
620	    their difference.  Initial state ``(c_0, 0)`` with ``c_0 ~ Bin(n, p0)``.
621	    ``gain`` is one mapping (the same law every generation) or a sequence of
622	    ``generations`` mappings (a schedule; the chain is then time-inhomogeneous
623	    and the DP uses generation ``g``'s kernel at step ``g``).
624	    Boundaries: candidates independent of the incumbent, gains i.i.d. across
625	    candidates within a generation, lattice capped at one.
626	    """
627	
628	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
629	    _check_generations(generations)
630	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
631	    schedule = _check_gain_schedule(gain, generations)
632	    levels = drift_levels(p0, step)
633	    top = len(levels) - 1
634	    tables: dict[tuple, tuple[list, list]] = {}
635	
636	    def table(gain_law):
637	        key = tuple(sorted(gain_law.items()))
638	        if key in tables:
639	            return tables[key]
640	        stay_power, joint = [], []
641	        for level in range(top + 1):
642	            parts = {m: _binomial_pmf(items, levels[min(top, level + m)]) for m in gain_law}
643	            mixture = [sum(gain_law[m] * parts[m][j] for m in gain_law) for j in range(items + 1)]
644	            cdf, running = [], Q(0)
645	            for mass in mixture:
646	                running += mass
647	                cdf.append(running)
648	            best = [cdf[j]**candidates - (cdf[j - 1]**candidates if j else Q(0))
649	                    for j in range(items + 1)]
650	            per_count = []
651	            for j in range(items + 1):
652	                if mixture[j]:
653	                    per_count.append({m: best[j] * gain_law[m] * parts[m][j] / mixture[j]
654	                                      for m in gain_law})
655	                else:
656	                    per_count.append({m: Q(0) for m in gain_law})
657	            joint.append(per_count)
658	            stay_power.append([cdf[j]**candidates for j in range(items + 1)])
659	        tables[key] = (stay_power, joint)
660	        return tables[key]
661	
662	    current = {(c, 0): mass for c, mass in enumerate(_binomial_pmf(items, levels[0])) if mass}
663	    history, acceptance, true_gain_acceptance = [current], [], []
664	    for gain_law in schedule:
665	        stay_power, joint = table(gain_law)
666	        following, accepted, accepted_with_gain = {}, Q(0), Q(0)
667	        for (c, level), mass in current.items():
668	            cap = min(items, c + threshold[c])
669	            stay = stay_power[level][cap]
670	            following[(c, level)] = following.get((c, level), Q(0)) + mass * stay
671	            accepted += mass * (1 - stay)
672	            for j in range(cap + 1, items + 1):
673	                for m, prob in joint[level][j].items():
674	                    if prob:
675	                        key = (j, min(top, level + m))
676	                        following[key] = following.get(key, Q(0)) + mass * prob
677	                        if m > 0 and level < top:
678	                            accepted_with_gain += mass * prob
679	        current = {key: mass for key, mass in following.items() if mass}
680	        history.append(current)
681	        acceptance.append(accepted)
682	        true_gain_acceptance.append(accepted_with_gain)
683	
684	    reported = [sum(mass * c for (c, _), mass in dist.items()) / items for dist in history]
685	    true = [sum(mass * levels[level] for (_, level), mass in dist.items()) for dist in history]
686	    return {
687	        "items": items, "candidates": candidates, "p0": levels[0], "step": Q(step),
688	        "gain_schedule": schedule, "threshold": threshold, "generations": generations,
689	        "levels": levels,
690	        "expected_reported": reported, "expected_true": true,
691	        "readout_gap": [r - t for r, t in zip(reported, true)],
692	        "acceptance_probability": acceptance,
693	        "true_gain_acceptance_probability": true_gain_acceptance,
694	        "expected_acceptances": sum(acceptance, Q(0)),
695	        "expected_true_gain_acceptances": sum(true_gain_acceptance, Q(0)),
696	        "mass_per_generation": [sum(dist.values(), Q(0)) for dist in history],
697	        "final_distribution": {f"{c},{level}": mass for (c, level), mass in sorted(history[-1].items())},
698	        "state_history": history,
699	    }
700

703	# one generation, gate versus naive, under a fixed true gain
704	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
705	
706	def one_step_gap_change(items, candidates, p_inc, delta, c, t) -> dict[str, object]:
707	    """One generation from incumbent count ``c`` and true value ``p_inc``
708	    when every candidate has true probability ``p_inc + delta``.
709	
710	    ``M`` is the max of ``K`` i.i.d. ``Bin(n, p_inc + delta)`` counts.  On
711	    acceptance the reported score changes by ``(M - c) / n`` and the true
712	    value by ``delta``; otherwise neither moves.  Naive accepts iff
713	    ``M > c``; the gate iff ``M > c + t``.  Since
714	    ``1{M > c} - 1{M > c + t} = 1{c < M <= c + t}``,
715	
716	        naive_change - gate_change
717	            = E[ ((M - c) / n - delta) * 1{c < M <= c + t} ].
718	
719	    On the window ``1 <= M - c <= t``, so the integrand lies in
720	    ``[1/n - delta, t/n - delta]``: (i) ``delta <= 1/n`` makes it ``>= 0``
721	    (the gate lowers the one-generation gap change); (ii)
722	    ``delta >= t/n`` makes it ``<= 0`` (the gate raises it); (iii) in
723	    between the sign depends on the law of ``M`` on the window.  When both
724	    (i) and (ii) hold (``t <= 1`` and ``delta = 1/n``, or ``t = 0``) the
725	    difference is exactly zero.  ``t`` is the gate's threshold at ``c``.
726	    All quantities are exact rationals.
727	    """
728	
729	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
730	    p_inc = _check_probability(p_inc, "p_inc")
731	    if type(delta) is bool or not isinstance(delta, (int, Q)) or delta < 0 or p_inc + delta > 1:
732	        raise ValueError("delta must be a non-negative Fraction with p_inc + delta <= 1")
733	    delta = Q(delta)
734	    _check_state(c, items)
735	    if type(t) is not int or t < 0:
736	        raise ValueError("t must be a non-negative integer")
737	    best = best_of_pmf(items, candidates, p_inc + delta)
738	
739	    def change(cap):
740	        return sum((Q(j - c, items) - delta) * best[j] for j in range(cap + 1, items + 1))
741	
742	    naive, gate = change(c), change(min(items, c + t))
743	    window = range(c + 1, min(items, c + t) + 1)
744	    window_integral = sum(((Q(j - c, items) - delta) * best[j] for j in window), Q(0))
745	    window_mass = sum((best[j] for j in window), Q(0))
746	    case_i, case_ii = delta <= Q(1, items), delta >= Q(t, items)
747	    predicted = ("zero" if case_i and case_ii else "nonnegative" if case_i
748	                 else "nonpositive" if case_ii else "undetermined")
749	    return {"items": items, "candidates": candidates, "p_inc": p_inc, "delta": delta,
750	            "c": c, "t": t, "naive_change": naive, "gate_change": gate,
751	            "difference": naive - gate, "window_integral": window_integral,
752	            "window_mass": window_mass,
753	            "case_i_delta_at_most_one_over_n": case_i,
754	            "case_ii_delta_at_least_t_over_n": case_ii,
755	            "predicted_sign_of_difference": predicted}
756	
757	
758	def drift_gap_increment_from_one_step(trajectory, generation) -> Q:
759	    """``rho_{g+1} - rho_g`` of a fixed-gain drift trajectory recomputed from
760	    ``one_step_gap_change`` on the state law at ``g``: the consistency
761	    check between the one-step theorem and the drift DP.  Requires the
762	    gain law ``{1: 1}`` (every candidate carries exactly one lattice step)."""
763	
764	    schedule = trajectory["gain_schedule"]
765	    if not 0 <= generation < len(schedule) or schedule[generation] != {1: Q(1)}:
766	        raise ValueError("generation must index a fixed-gain generation of the trajectory")
767	    items, candidates = trajectory["items"], trajectory["candidates"]
768	    levels, threshold = trajectory["levels"], trajectory["threshold"]
769	    top = len(levels) - 1
770	    increment = Q(0)
771	    for (c, level), mass in trajectory["state_history"][generation].items():
772	        nxt = min(top, level + 1)
773	        step = one_step_gap_change(items, candidates, levels[level], levels[nxt] - levels[level],
774	                                   c, threshold[c])
775	        increment += mass * step["gate_change"]
776	    return increment

784	    last = len(trajectory["expected_reported"]) - 1

786	            or not 0 <= start < end <= last):

790	def phantom_share(trajectory, start, end) -> dict[str, object]:
791	    """``1 - (true gain) / (reported gain)`` over generations ``start..end``.
792	
793	    ``None`` when the reported gain is zero.  Under the null the true gain is
794	    zero, so the share is one whenever anything was reported as gained.
795	    """
796	
797	    _check_window(trajectory, start, end)
798	    reported = trajectory["expected_reported"][end] - trajectory["expected_reported"][start]
799	    true = trajectory["expected_true"][end] - trajectory["expected_true"][start]
800	    share = None if reported == 0 else 1 - true / reported
801	    return {"start": start, "end": end, "reported_gain": reported,
802	            "true_gain": true, "phantom_share": share}

805	def late_early_ratio(trajectory, split) -> dict[str, object]:
806	    """Gain over ``split..G`` divided by gain over ``0..split``, for reported
807	    and for true value; the simulation's P5 quantity."""

930	def brute_force_drift_distribution(items, candidates, p0, step, gain, threshold,
931	                                   generations) -> dict[tuple[int, int], Q]:
932	    """Enumerate every gain draw and every item outcome of the drift model,
933	    weighting each path by its exact probability, and tally the final
934	    ``(count, level)`` state."""
935	
936	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
937	    _check_generations(generations)
938	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
939	    schedule = _check_gain_schedule(gain, generations)
940	    levels = drift_levels(p0, step)
941	    top = len(levels) - 1
942	    draws = generations * candidates
943	    bits = items * (1 + draws)
944	    supports = [sorted(schedule[g]) for g in range(generations) for _ in range(candidates)]
945	    combinations = 1
946	    for support in supports:
947	        combinations *= len(support)
948	    if bits > _BRUTE_FORCE_BIT_LIMIT or combinations > _BRUTE_FORCE_GAIN_COMBINATIONS:
949	        raise ValueError("brute force limited to 16 item outcomes and 64 gain combinations")
950	    distribution: dict[tuple[int, int], Q] = {}
951	    for gains in product(*supports):
952	        gain_weight = Q(1)
953	        for index, m in enumerate(gains):
954	            gain_weight *= schedule[index // candidates][m]
955	        for outcome in product((0, 1), repeat=bits):
956	            weight = gain_weight * _path_weight(outcome[:items], levels[0])
957	            c, level, position = sum(outcome[:items]), 0, items
958	            for g in range(generations):
959	                best, best_multiple = -1, None
960	                for k in range(candidates):
961	                    m = gains[g * candidates + k]
962	                    block = outcome[position:position + items]
963	                    position += items
964	                    weight *= _path_weight(block, levels[min(top, level + m)])
965	                    count = sum(block)
966	                    if count > best:
967	                        best, best_multiple = count, m
968	                if best > c + threshold[c]:
969	                    c, level = best, min(top, level + best_multiple)
970	            if weight:
971	                distribution[(c, level)] = distribution.get((c, level), Q(0)) + weight

978	def brute_force_mutation_distribution(items, candidates, p, q, threshold, generations) -> list[Q]:
979	    """Enumerate the incumbent's item outcomes and, for every candidate item,
980	    one of three symbols (copy the incumbent's outcome, redraw and fail,
981	    redraw and succeed, weights ``1 - q``, ``q (1 - p)``, ``q p``), tracking
982	    outcome *vectors* rather than counts so that the Markov-on-count claim
983	    is itself under test.  Ties among candidates go to the first index."""
984	
985	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
986	    _check_generations(generations)
987	    p = _check_probability(p)
988	    q = _check_probability(q, "q")
989	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
990	    symbols = items * generations * candidates
991	    if 2**items * 3**symbols > _MUTATION_BRUTE_FORCE_PATH_LIMIT:
992	        raise ValueError("brute force limited to 2^16 paths")
993	    symbol_weight = (1 - q, q * (1 - p), q * p)
994	    distribution = [Q(0)] * (items + 1)
995	    for incumbent in product((0, 1), repeat=items):
996	        base = _path_weight(incumbent, p)
997	        for choice in product((0, 1, 2), repeat=symbols):
998	            weight = base
999	            for symbol in choice:
1000	                weight *= symbol_weight[symbol]
1001	            if not weight:
1002	                continue
1003	            vector, c, position = incumbent, sum(incumbent), 0
1004	            for _ in range(generations):
1005	                best, best_vector = -1, None
1006	                for _ in range(candidates):
1007	                    block = choice[position:position + items]
1008	                    position += items
1009	                    candidate = tuple(vector[j] if block[j] == 0 else block[j] - 1
1010	                                      for j in range(items))
1011	                    count = sum(candidate)
1012	                    if count > best:
1013	                        best, best_vector = count, candidate
1014	                if best > c + threshold[c]:
1015	                    vector, c = best_vector, best
1016	            distribution[c] += weight
1017	    return distribution

1021	# Proposition 8: naive versus gated chains under a fixed true gain
1022	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
1023	#
1024	# Fix the gain law {1: 1} (every accepted candidate carries one lattice
1025	# step; a deterministic multiple m is the same chain on the coarser lattice
1026	# p0 + i m step).  Write P for the naive kernel and Q for the kernel of any
1027	# threshold rule t >= 0 on states x = (c, i), u_k = P^k f, w_k = Q^k f.
1028	#
1029	# Theorem (true value).  For every non-decreasing phi on levels, f = phi(i),
1030	# every t >= 0, every non-decreasing level function and every state x:
1031	# w_k(x) <= u_k(x) for all k.  Proof in three steps, all finite inductions.
1032	#   (M1)/(M2)  The naive iterates u_k are non-increasing in c and
1033	#     non-decreasing in i.  Downward induction on the level: (M1) at level l
1034	#     follows from (M2) at level l by the first-divergence identity
1035	#     u_k(c,l) - u_k(c+1,l) = sum_s F_l(c)^(s-1) pi_l(c+1) [u_{k-s}(c+1,l+1)
1036	#     - u_{k-s}(c+1,l)]; (M2) at level l follows from (M1) at level l+2 by
1037	#     expanding the lower chain two jumps and the upper chain one jump: the
1038	#     upper waits less (sigma <=_st tau), lands below the lower's second
1039	#     landing (M_{l+1} | > c <=_st M_{l+1} | > x for x > c), and u(., l+2)
1040	#     is non-increasing in the count and non-decreasing in time.  Base: at
1041	#     the top levels u is constant in c or equals phi(l) + (phi(l+1) -
1042	#     phi(l)) (1 - F_l(c)^k).
1043	#   (S)  w_k(c,i) <= u_k(j,i+1) for c < j <= a(c) = min(n, c + t(c)): one
1044	#     gated step, then (S)_{k-1} on the self-loop, the theorem at k-1 on the
1045	#     landings J > a(c) >= j, (M1) to pull every landing back to j, and
1046	#     u_{k-1} <= u_k.
1047	#   (D)  Couple both chains on the same draws from x; they agree until the
1048	#     first generation at which the naive accepts a draw M in (c, a(c)]
1049	#     that the gate rejects, and then the difference is u_{k-s}(M,i+1) -
1050	#     w_{k-s}(c,i) >= 0 by (S).
1051	# Corollary: the level is stochastically dominated (phi = 1{i >= l}) and
1052	# E[p(i_g)] is ordered, from every initial law, at every horizon.
1053	#
1054	# The count.  E[c_infinity] = n for the naive chain whenever p(1) > 0, so
1055	# the limit ordering is trivial; at finite horizons no proof is known.  The
1056	# routes that work for the level fail provably: the naive count iterates
1057	# are not monotone in c (a lower count earns a free level), so neither the
1058	# pathwise coupling, nor the gate-cone condition u_k(j,i+1) >= u_k(c,i) on
1059	# the naive iterates, nor the policy-improvement condition on the gated
1060	# iterates, nor the componentwise condition u_k(c,i) <= u_k(c',i') for
1061	# c <= c', i < i' holds (``dominance_structure_fixture`` records witnesses).
1062	# What holds on every enumerated cell, at every state and horizon, is the
1063	# ordering itself, its hitting-probability form P(c_k >= m), and (S) for
1064	# the count.  Lowering an arbitrary threshold is NOT monotone in general:
1065	# ``threshold_pair_counterexample`` gives two rules t <= t' with the higher
1066	# one ahead in true value.  All of this is finite evidence only.
1067

1072	    except TypeError:
1073	        raise ValueError("levels must be a sequence of rationals") from None
1074	    if (not levels or any(type(x) is bool or not isinstance(x, (int, Q)) or not 0 <= x <= 1 for x in levels)
1075	            or any(b < a for a, b in zip(levels, levels[1:]))):
1076	        raise ValueError("levels must be non-decreasing rationals in [0, 1]")

1090	def drift_kernel(items, candidates, levels, gain_law, threshold) -> dict[tuple[int, int], list[tuple[tuple[int, int], Q]]]:
1091	    """Exact one-generation kernel of the drift chain on ``(count, level)``.
1092	
1093	    ``kernel[(c, i)]`` lists ``((c', i'), probability)`` with the self-loop
1094	    first.  The same chain as ``drift_trajectory`` on the lattice ``levels``
1095	    (checked by test), with the joint law of the best count and its gain
1096	    written as ``gain[m] Bin(n, p(i+m))(j) S_j``, ``S_j = sum_{k=1}^K
1097	    F(j-1)^(k-1) F(j)^(K-k)`` summing the first-max tie rule over the index
1098	    of the winning candidate; ``mix(j) S_j = F(j)^K - F(j-1)^K``, so the
1099	    denominators stay powers of the binomial denominators.
1100	    """
1101	
1102	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
1103	    levels = _check_levels(levels)
1104	    gain_law = _check_gain(gain_law)
1105	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
1106	    top = len(levels) - 1
1107	    kernel = {}
1108	    for level in range(top + 1):
1109	        parts = {m: _cached_pmf(items, levels[min(top, level + m)]) for m in gain_law}
1110	        mixture = [sum(gain_law[m] * parts[m][j] for m in gain_law) for j in range(items + 1)]
1111	        cdf, running = [], Q(0)
1112	        for mass in mixture:
1113	            running += mass
1114	            cdf.append(running)
1115	        ties = []
1116	        for j in range(items + 1):
1117	            lower = cdf[j - 1] if j else Q(0)
1118	            ties.append(sum((lower**(k - 1) * cdf[j]**(candidates - k)
1119	                             for k in range(1, candidates + 1)), Q(0)))
1120	        for c in range(items + 1):
1121	            cap = min(items, c + threshold[c])
1122	            entries = [((c, level), cdf[cap]**candidates)]
1123	            for j in range(cap + 1, items + 1):
1124	                for m in gain_law:
1125	                    prob = gain_law[m] * parts[m][j] * ties[j]
1126	                    if prob:
1127	                        entries.append(((j, min(top, level + m)), prob))
1128	            kernel[(c, level)] = entries
1129	    return kernel

1141	def drift_expectations(items, candidates, levels, gain, threshold, generations,
1142	                       absorption_tolerance=None) -> dict[str, object]:
1143	    """``E[c_g] / n``, ``E[p(i_g)]`` and the absorbed mass for ``g = 0..G``.
1144	
1145	    The state law is propagated as integer numerators over one common
1146	    denominator (the lcm of the kernel's denominators, one factor per
1147	    generation), so no gcd is taken until an expectation is formed; the
1148	    values equal ``drift_trajectory``'s exactly (test).  With
1149	    ``absorption_tolerance`` the run stops at the first generation whose
1150	    mass on ``drift_absorbing_states`` is at least ``1 - tolerance``
1151	    (``stopped_at``); from then on each expectation can move by at most the
1152	    unabsorbed mass.  ``gain`` is one law or a schedule of length ``G``.
1153	    """
1154	
1155	    _check_items_candidates(items, candidates)
1156	    _check_generations(generations)
1157	    levels = _check_levels(levels)
1158	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
1159	    schedule = _check_gain_schedule(gain, generations)
1160	    if absorption_tolerance is not None:
1161	        absorption_tolerance = _check_probability(absorption_tolerance, "absorption_tolerance")
1162	    absorbing = drift_absorbing_states(items, levels, threshold)
1163	    initial = {(c, 0): mass for c, mass in enumerate(_cached_pmf(items, levels[0])) if mass}
1164	    denominator = lcm(*[mass.denominator for mass in initial.values()])
1165	    current = {x: int(mass * denominator) for x, mass in initial.items()}
1166	    kernels: dict[tuple, tuple[int, dict]] = {}
1167	    reported, true, absorbed = [], [], []
1168	
1169	    def record():
1170	        by_level = [0] * len(levels)
1171	        for (_, i), mass in current.items():
1172	            by_level[i] += mass
1173	        reported.append(Q(sum(mass * c for (c, _), mass in current.items()), denominator) / items)
1174	        true.append(sum((level * mass for level, mass in zip(levels, by_level) if mass), Q(0)) / denominator)
1175	        absorbed.append(Q(sum(mass for x, mass in current.items() if x in absorbing), denominator))
1176	
1177	    record()
1178	    stopped = None
1179	    for g, law in enumerate(schedule):
1180	        key = tuple(sorted(law.items()))
1181	        if key not in kernels:
1182	            kernel = drift_kernel(items, candidates, levels, law, threshold)
1183	            common = lcm(*[prob.denominator for entries in kernel.values() for _, prob in entries])
1184	            kernels[key] = (common, {x: [(y, int(prob * common)) for y, prob in entries]
1185	                                     for x, entries in kernel.items()})
1186	        common, integer_kernel = kernels[key]
1187	        following: dict[tuple[int, int], int] = {}
1188	        for x, mass in current.items():
1189	            for y, weight in integer_kernel[x]:
1190	                following[y] = following.get(y, 0) + mass * weight
1191	        current = {x: mass for x, mass in following.items() if mass}
1192	        denominator *= common
1193	        record()
1194	        if absorption_tolerance is not None and absorbed[-1] >= 1 - absorption_tolerance:
1195	            stopped = g + 1
1196	            break
1197	    return {"items": items, "candidates": candidates, "levels": levels, "threshold": threshold,
1198	            "generations": generations, "generations_run": len(reported) - 1,
1199	            "expected_reported": reported, "expected_true": true, "absorbed_mass": absorbed,
1200	            "stopped_at": stopped}

1203	def drift_limit(items, candidates, levels, gain_law, threshold) -> dict[str, object]:
1204	    """Exact ``g -> infinity`` expectations of a constant-law drift chain.
1205	
1206	    Jumps raise the count, so the states ordered by count form a DAG with
1207	    self-loops; processing counts from ``n`` downward, the limit value at a
1208	    transient state is the mean of the limit values at its landings under
1209	    the law of the jump given that it leaves.  A state that cannot leave
1210	    (``c + t(c) >= n``, or a zero leaving probability) keeps its own value.
1211	    ``by_state[(c, i)] = (E[c_inf], E[p(i_inf)])`` from that state;
1212	    ``expected_reported`` and ``expected_true`` average over the initial
1213	    law ``(Bin(n, p(0)), 0)``.
1214	    """
1215	
1216	    kernel = drift_kernel(items, candidates, levels, gain_law, threshold)
1217	    levels = _check_levels(levels)
1218	    threshold = _check_threshold(threshold, items)
1219	    top = len(levels) - 1
1220	    by_state: dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[Q, Q]] = {}
1221	    for c in range(items, -1, -1):
1222	        for i in range(top + 1):
1223	            x = (c, i)
1224	            stay = kernel[x][0][1]
1225	            if c + threshold[c] >= items or stay == 1:
1226	                by_state[x] = (Q(c), levels[i])
1227	                continue
1228	            leave = 1 - stay
1229	            by_state[x] = (sum((prob * by_state[y][0] for y, prob in kernel[x][1:]), Q(0)) / leave,
1230	                           sum((prob * by_state[y][1] for y, prob in kernel[x][1:]), Q(0)) / leave)
1231	    initial = _cached_pmf(items, levels[0])
1232	    return {"by_state": by_state,
1233	            "expected_reported": sum((initial[c] * by_state[(c, 0)][0] for c in range(items + 1)), Q(0)) / items,
1234	            "expected_true": sum((initial[c] * by_state[(c, 0)][1] for c in range(items + 1)), Q(0))}

1237	def kernel_iterates(kernel, f, horizon) -> list[dict[tuple[int, int], Q]]:
1238	    """``P^k f`` on every state for ``k = 0..horizon``: ``P^k f(x)`` is the
1239	    expectation of ``f`` after ``k`` generations from ``x``."""
1240	
1241	    _check_generations(horizon)
1242	    current = {x: Q(f(x)) for x in kernel}
1243	    history = [current]
1244	    for _ in range(horizon):
1245	        current = {x: sum((prob * current[y] for y, prob in entries), Q(0))
1246	                   for x, entries in kernel.items()}
1247	        history.append(current)
1248	    return history

1266	def dominance_search(gain, items_grid, candidates_grid, z_grid, p0_grid, step_grid,
1267	                     horizon, tolerance) -> dict[str, object]:
1268	    """Naive versus ``z``-gate on every cell of the grid: exact expectations
1269	    at every generation up to ``horizon`` (stopping early once both chains
1270	    are within ``tolerance`` of absorption) and, for a constant law, the
1271	    exact limits.  ``gain`` is a constant law or a callable ``horizon ->
1272	    schedule``.  Records the first generation at which the gate is above
1273	    the naive chain in either expectation, with exact values, or ``None``.
1274	    """
1275	
1276	    rows, violations, limit_violations, generations, absorbed_cells = {}, [], [], 0, 0
1277	    constant = isinstance(gain, dict)
1278	    for p0 in p0_grid:
1279	        for step in step_grid:
1280	            levels = drift_levels(p0, step)
1281	            for items in items_grid:
1282	                for candidates in candidates_grid:
1283	                    for z in z_grid:
1284	                        thresholds = {"naive": naive_threshold(items), "gate": gate_threshold(items, z)}
1285	                        schedule = gain if constant else gain(horizon)
1286	                        runs = {name: drift_expectations(items, candidates, levels, schedule, thr,
1287	                                                         horizon, tolerance)
1288	                                for name, thr in thresholds.items()}
1289	                        naive, gate = runs["naive"], runs["gate"]
1290	                        compared = min(naive["generations_run"], gate["generations_run"])
1291	                        generations += compared
1292	                        key = f"gain={'law' if constant else 'schedule'},p0={p0},step={step},n={items},K={candidates},z={z}"
1293	                        first = next((g for g in range(compared + 1)
1294	                                      if naive["expected_reported"][g] < gate["expected_reported"][g]
1295	                                      or naive["expected_true"][g] < gate["expected_true"][g]), None)
1296	                        if first is not None:
1297	                            violations.append({"cell": key, "generation": first,
1298	                                               "naive": (naive["expected_reported"][first], naive["expected_true"][first]),
1299	                                               "gate": (gate["expected_reported"][first], gate["expected_true"][first])})
1300	                        limits = None
1301	                        if constant:
1302	                            ln = drift_limit(items, candidates, levels, gain, thresholds["naive"])
1303	                            lg = drift_limit(items, candidates, levels, gain, thresholds["gate"])
1304	                            limits = {"naive": (ln["expected_reported"], ln["expected_true"]),
1305	                                      "gate": (lg["expected_reported"], lg["expected_true"])}
1306	                            if (ln["expected_reported"] < lg["expected_reported"]
1307	                                    or ln["expected_true"] < lg["expected_true"]):
1308	                                limit_violations.append({"cell": key, **limits})
1309	                        absorbed_cells += naive["stopped_at"] is not None and gate["stopped_at"] is not None
1310	                        rows[key] = {
1311	                            "generations_compared": compared,
1312	                            "stopped_at": {"naive": naive["stopped_at"], "gate": gate["stopped_at"]},
1313	                            "first_violation_generation": first,
1314	                            "reported_at_end": {k: _render_float(r["expected_reported"][compared]) for k, r in runs.items()},
1315	                            "true_at_end": {k: _render_float(r["expected_true"][compared]) for k, r in runs.items()},
1316	                            "limit": None if limits is None else {k: tuple(_render_float(v) for v in vals)
1317	                                                                  for k, vals in limits.items()},
1318	                        }
1319	    return {"cells": len(rows), "generations_compared": generations,
1320	            "cells_absorbed_within_horizon": absorbed_cells,
1321	            "violations": violations, "limit_violations": limit_violations,
1322	            "first_violation": violations[0] if violations else None,
1323	            "horizon": horizon, "absorption_tolerance": tolerance,
1324	            "rows": rows, "note": "end-of-horizon and limit values are float renderings; comparisons are exact"}

1550	def bound_fixture() -> dict[str, object]:
1551	    """Hoeffding and Bernstein bounds against the exact DP gap on every null
1552	    cell and generation, in floats under ``BOUND_TOLERANCE``, with the ratio
1553	    of the exact gap to the Gaussian scale ``sqrt(2 ln(GK+1) p(1-p)/n)``
1554	    tabulated at the report generations."""
1555	
1556	    cells, ratios = {}, []
1557	    flags = {"hoeffding_holds": True, "bernstein_holds": True,
1558	             "hoeffding_tighter_at_p_half": True, "bernstein_tighter_somewhere_at_p_quarter": False,
1559	             "ratio_below_one": True, "bound_exceeds_cap_somewhere": False}
1560	    tighter = {"hoeffding": 0, "bernstein": 0}
1561	    for items in NULL_ITEMS:
1562	        for candidates in NULL_CANDIDATES:
1563	            for p in NULL_PROBABILITIES:
1564	                gaps = reuse_trajectory(items, candidates, p, naive_threshold(items), HORIZON)["readout_gap"]
1565	                cap, table, cap_crossing = float(1 - p), {}, None
1566	                for g in range(HORIZON + 1):
1567	                    bounds = naive_gap_bounds(items, candidates, p, g)
1568	                    gap = float(gaps[g])
1569	                    flags["hoeffding_holds"] &= gap <= bounds["hoeffding"] + BOUND_TOLERANCE
1570	                    flags["bernstein_holds"] &= gap <= bounds["bernstein"] + BOUND_TOLERANCE
1571	                    if g:
1572	                        # At p = 1/2 the Gaussian scale equals the Hoeffding
1573	                        # bound, so Bernstein exceeds it by ln m / (3 n).
1574	                        bernstein_tighter = bounds["bernstein"] < bounds["hoeffding"] - BOUND_TOLERANCE
1575	                        tighter["bernstein" if bernstein_tighter else "hoeffding"] += 1
1576	                        if p == Q(1, 2):
1577	                            flags["hoeffding_tighter_at_p_half"] &= not bernstein_tighter
1578	                        else:
1579	                            flags["bernstein_tighter_somewhere_at_p_quarter"] |= bernstein_tighter
1580	                        if cap_crossing is None and bounds["hoeffding"] > cap:
1581	                            cap_crossing = g
1582	                    if g in REPORT_GENERATIONS:
1583	                        ratio = gap / bounds["gaussian_scale"]
1584	                        ratios.append(ratio)
1585	                        flags["ratio_below_one"] &= ratio < 1
1586	                        table[g] = {"exact_gap": gaps[g], "gap_float": gap,
1587	                                    "hoeffding": bounds["hoeffding"],
1588	                                    "bernstein": bounds["bernstein"],
1589	                                    "gaussian_scale": bounds["gaussian_scale"],
1590	                                    "ratio_gap_to_gaussian_scale": ratio,
1591	                                    "hoeffding_slack": bounds["hoeffding"] - gap}

28	def _pmf(items, p):
29	    return [Q(comb(items, j)) * p**j * (1 - p)**(items - j) for j in range(items + 1)]

32	def _count_enumeration(items, candidates, p, threshold, generations):
33	    """Independent enumeration over count tuples with binomial weights."""
34	
35	    pmf, distribution = _pmf(items, p), [Q(0)] * (items + 1)
36	    for counts in product(range(items + 1), repeat=1 + generations * candidates):
37	        mass = Q(1)
38	        for j in counts:
39	            mass *= pmf[j]
40	        c = counts[0]
41	        for g in range(generations):
42	            best = max(counts[1 + g * candidates:1 + (g + 1) * candidates])
43	            if best > c + threshold[c]:
44	                c = best
45	        distribution[c] += mass
46	    return distribution

    naive level while the naive count is still below ``m``.  Returns the
